import os,re,json,itertools,math
from collections import defaultdict, Counter
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))
Demos=['Demo pair %d'%k for k in range(1,6)]
# Hypothesis set A: cell 5 iff (#markers at odd Manhattan distance) is odd — previously said fails on ALL demos; verify on demo5 & check tie handling
for nm in Demos:
    I=G[nm+' input']; O=G[nm+' output']
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0]); bg=I[0][0]
    sp=[(i,j) for i in range(H) for j in range(W) if I[i][j]!=bg]
    cnt=0
    for i in range(H):
        for j in range(W):
            if I[i][j]==bg:
                nd=sum(abs(i-r)+abs(j-c)%2==1 for r,c in sp)
                exp=(nd%2==1)
                if exp!=(O[i][j]==5): cnt+=1
    tot=sum(1 for i in range(H) for j in range(W) if I[i][j]==bg)
    print(nm,'odd-man-count-parity mismatches:',cnt,'of',tot)

import itertools,os,re,json
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))
Demos=['Demo pair %d'%k for k in range(1,6)]
# Print per-cell features for ALL demos in compact tables: man&cheb to each marker, F?, and min/man
print('feature study: columns = (cell,min_man over markers,n_tie,cheb_at_min,diff man-cheb, second_min_gap, F?)')
for nm in Demos:
    I=G[nm+' input']; O=G[nm+' output']
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0]); bg=I[0][0]
    sp=[(i,j) for i in range(H) for j in range(W) if I[i][j]!=bg]
    print('===',nm,'markers',sp,'dims',(H,W))
    for i in range(H):
        for j in range(W):
            if I[i][j]!=bg: continue
            ds=[(abs(i-r)+abs(j-c), max(abs(i-r),abs(j-c))) for r,c in sp]
            dm=sorted(ds,key=lambda x:x[0])
            mnd=dm[0][0]; nts=sum(1 for d,_ in ds if d==mnd)
            gaps=[]
            for k in range(1,len(dm)): gaps.append(dm[k][0]-dm[k-1][0])
            f=F if False else None
            pred=O[i][j]==5
            print(f'{(i,j)} dm={mnd} n={nts} g={gaps} {"F" if pred else "."}')

# Zigzag path model (demo 5, marker (15,7) down-left): steps pattern: V2,H2,V2,H2... alternating run length 2 until hitting edge; also short up arm (13..14, col7) len 2.
# Check demo1 shapes vs zigzag of run length 2 in various dirs. Also markers emit in all 8 directions? Let's just attempt generic algorithm:
# From each marker, for each direction d in 8 dirs, walk: while in bounds and cell==bg, step along dir; every k steps turn? But demo1 shows many horizontal segments adjacent... e.g. row0: ### at 3,6-9 etc.
# Simpler hypothesis: paint ALL cells whose chebyshev distance to some marker is odd?? No (rejected). 
# Alternative: the paths are diagonals! Look at demo 1 mask rows0-2: '...#....#.#' then '.###..###.M' — diagonal stripes going down-right? Row r has #s; check if paints form anti-diagonals: cells with manhattan dist from marker? For marker (3,1): manhattan rings... but we saw parity fails.
# Try: for each marker, draw rays that alternate between the two perpendicular... Actually visualize: staircase = repeated [dir A x2, dir B x2]. In demo5 bottom arm: it goes DOWN 2, LEFT 2, DOWN 2, LEFT 2, ... That IS a diagonal-like stair toward down-left, one "cell" per 2x2 block. Similarly top arm goes UP 2 then... only 2 because row -1 edge. And right side of that arm? At (17,7)? included. Up: (14,7),(13,7): vertical up 2.
# Demo1 marker (1,10): row0 has #(0,3),(0,8),(0,10); row1 '#.' pattern cols1-3,6-8 then M; row2 cols2,6,9... Looks like multiple arms from each marker.
# Algorithm candidate: for each marker, for each of 8 directions, walk: move straight until hitting grid edge or another painted/marker... no, that would fill rectangles, not zigzags.
# New idea: maybe each marker emits a zigzag along ONE diagonal direction determined by something, plus perpendicular arms. Let me extract actual paths as connected components in masks and print them as coordinate lists per marker, then eyeball.
from collections import deque
def comps(I,O,bg):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0]); seen=set(); out=[]
    for i in range(H):
        for j in range(W):
            if (i,j) not in seen and O[i][j]==5:
                q=deque([(i,j)]); c={(i,j)}; seen.add((i,j))
                while q:
                    r,cc=q.popleft()
                    for dr,dc in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                        nr,nc=r+dr,c+dc
                        if 0<=nr<H and 0<=nc<W and (nr,nc) not in seen and O[nr][nc]==5:
                            seen.add((nr,nc)); c.add((nr,nc)); q.append((nr,nc))
                out.append(c)
    return out
for nm in ['Demo pair %d'%k for k in range(1,6)]:
    I=G[nm+' input']; O=G[nm+' output']
    bg=I[0][0]; H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    ms=[(i,j) for i in range(H) for j in range(W) if I[i][j]!=bg]
    for comp in comps(I,O,bg):
        near=[m for m in ms if any(abs(m[0]-r)+abs(m[1]-c)<=1 for r,c in comp)]
        print(nm,'marker-near',near,'size',len(comp),'cells',sorted(comp))

from math import gcd as GCD
def solve(I):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0]); bgc=I[0][0]
    ms=[(i,j) for i in range(H) for j in range(W) if I[i][j]!=bgc]
    out=[[0]*W for _ in range(H)]
    for r in range(H):
        for c in range(W):
            if I[r][c]!=bgc: continue
            dmin=min(abs(r-mr)+abs(c-mc) for mr,mc in ms)
            nb=[m for m in ms if abs(r-m[0])+abs(c-m[1])==dmin]
            # nearest pair (two markers at same min dist): paint iff cell is on segment between them
            if len(nb)==1: out[r][c]=5
            elif len(nb)>1:
                p,q=nb[0],nb[1]
                dy,dx=q[0]-p[0],q[1]-p[1]
                g=GCD(abs(dy),abs(dx)) or 1
                ok=False
                # check collinear with these two and in-between
                rr,cc=r,c
                # parametric: exists t such that (r,c)=(p+t*(q-p)/g?) only exact line: cross==0 & bounding box
                inline=(rr-p[0])*dx-(cc-p[1])*dy==0
                if inline and min(p[0],q[0])<=rr<=max(p[0],q[0]) and min(p[1],q[1])<=cc<=max(p[1],q[1]): ok=True

    return out

import os,re,json,itertools
from collections import defaultdict
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load()
from math import gcd as GCD
def f(I):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0]); bgc=I[0][0]
    ms=[(i,j) for i in range(H) for j in range(W) if I[i][j]!=bgc]
    ss=set()
    for a in range(len(ms)):
        for b_ in range(a+1,len(ms)):
            p,q=ms[a],ms[b_]
            if p==q: continue
            dy,dx=q[0]-p[0],q[1]-p[1]
            g=GCD(abs(dy),abs(dx))
            if g==0: continue
            sr,sc=dy//g,dx//g
            r,c=p
            while (r,c)!=q:
                r+=sr; c+=sc; ss.add((r,c))
    out=[[5 if (r,c) in ss else (I[r][c] if I[r][c]!=bgc else 0) for c in range(W)] for r in range(H)]
    return out
for k in range(1,9):
    P=f(G[f'Demo pair {k} input']); O=G[f'Demo pair {k} output']
    eq=sum(1 for r in range(len(P)) for c in range(len(P[0])) if P[r][c]==O[r][c])
    print(k,'correct',eq,'of',len(P)*len(P[0]))

from collections import defaultdict
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load()
# Hypothesis: paint background cell iff it lies strictly between two markers on a straight line (any slope incl diagonal).
def pred(I,O):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0]); bgc=I[0][0]
    ms=[(i,j) for i in range(H) for j in range(W) if I[i][j]!=bgc]
    out=[[0]*W for _ in range(H)]
    for r in range(H):
        for c in range(W):
            if I[r][c]!=bgc: continue
            # candidate slopes dr,dc from pairs of markers
            hits=False
            for mr1,mc1 in ms:
                for mr2,mc2 in ms:
                    if mr1==mr2 and mc1==mc2: continue
                    dr=(mr1-mr2); dc=(mc1-mc2)
                    g=gcd(abs(dr),abs(dc)); dr//=g; dc//=g
                    r1,c1,r2,c2=min(mr1,mr2),min(mc1,mc2),max(mr1,mr2),max(mc1,mc2)
                    # walk from nearer marker toward other
                    step=(1 if mr1<mr2 else -1, 1 if mc1<mc2 else -1)
                    rr,cc=r1,c1; inside=False
                    while rr<r2 or cc>c2:
                        rr+=step[0]; cc+=step[1]
                        if abs(rr-r)<=1 and abs(cc-c)<=1: 
                            pass
                    # simpler: cell between iff sign matches
                    sgn_r=(mr1-r)*(mr2-r); sgn_c=(mc1-c)*(mc2-c)
                    if sgn_r<=0 and sgn_c>=0 and sgn_r*sgn_c==0:

                    sgn_r=(mr1-r)*(mr2-r); sgn_c=(mc1-c)*(mc2-c)
                    if sgn_r<=0 and sgn_c<=0: hits=True; break
            out[r][c]=5 if hits else bgc
    return out

    cnt=Counter(x for row in inp for x in row)

    five=[(r,c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if exp[r][c]==5]
    print('pair',i,'frame',fc,'seeds',seeds)
    return inp,exp,fc,seeds,five,h,w
for i in [1]:
